html:
The Jiahui are a small Indigenous people of the southern Amazon, in the Brazilian state of Amazonas near Humaitá. They speak a Kawahib language of the Tupi-Guarani branch, close to that of the Tenharim and the Parintintin.

Rubber tappers of the rubber boom and disease brought them close to extinction in the 1900s; at one point only a handful of families survived. The Trans-Amazonian Highway, built through the region in the 1970s, brought settlers and loggers. Their land was recognised as an Indigenous territory in the 2000s, and their numbers are slowly growing again.
